fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly on both sides to help arriving units identify the access point without delay.
• Trim vegetation along the sides of the access drive to allow full-width vehicle passage and open sightlines for approaching units.
• Clear a turnaround area or pull-off near the residence so emergency vehicles are not blocked by other responding units or parked vehicles.
• Move or designate a consistent location for parked vehicles away from the access drive to keep it clear during an emergency response.
• Trim shrubs and trees near the detached structure so responders can reach and work around it without obstruction.
• Cut back dense vegetation along the side yards to allow responders to move between the front and rear of the property on foot.
• Keep a gate or opening in the perimeter fencing on at least one side of the property to allow responder access when the main drive is blocked.
• If the perimeter fence has a gate, keep it unlocked or secured with a lock compatible with a Knox box or rapid-entry system.
• Install a Knox box or rapid-entry key storage at the driveway entrance if any gates require a key to open.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim back all shrubs and plants that are growing directly against or touching the house walls.
• Thin the tree clusters near the structure to create open gaps between tree canopies and the roofline.
• Remove low-hanging branches from trees close to the house to reduce the path fire could take from the ground up into the trees.
• Separate the mixed vegetation areas surrounding the structure by clearing a visible open band of ground between the plants and the building.
• Keep scattered shrubs on the property cut low and spaced apart so they do not form a connected mass of plants leading toward the structure.
• Clear dead leaves, twigs, and plant debris from around the base of the structure regularly.
• Thin scattered trees near the house so their canopies do not touch or overlap with each other or with the roof.
• Keep the single access driveway clear of overhanging branches and encroaching shrubs along both sides so emergency vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it remains easy to locate under smoky or low-visibility conditions.
• Move any wood piles, stored materials, or combustible items away from the sides of the house and into open areas away from the structure.
• Clear vegetation along the edges of the driveway back far enough to allow a vehicle to pull to the side if needed.
